Subject: Nordic Retail discovery — latency/streaming SLOs + next steps

Hi Anna — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the proposed operational plan so we can get your perf qualification started next week.

Call highlights (short):
- Targeted user-facing SLO: p95 & p99 for completion latency. You indicated p95 <= 80ms and p99 <= 220ms for short chat replies (~150 tokens).
- Streaming: must support streaming token-by-token for live search UX (client consumes partial results).
- Concurrency/throughput: expected steady-state 180 QPS with 800 concurrent active sessions during peak, burst to ~1200 for promotions.
- Quality bar: SQuAD-style top-1 correctness acceptable; we'll surface quality delta if we test smaller quantized variants.

Immediate asks / next steps I propose:
1) We run a focused perf qualification (hosted) using your sample payloads — includes both streaming and non-streaming flows.
2) Provide 48h of realistic traffic trace (or synthetic load profile) — sample format attached.
3) Redwood team to produce a cost/perf plan with recommended levers: batching window, KV cache policy, quantization profiles, and model variant choices.
4) Schedule a 60-min runbook walkthrough after the first test run (Jordan will lead on runtime config).

Attachments: perf-qualification-checklist.xlsx (checklist + required artifacts), sample-payloads.json.

Proposed timeline:
- Tues 5/19: Receive sample payloads/trace from you.
- Wed 5/20: Redwood engineers run initial qualification (streaming + p99 sample).
- Thu 5/21: Review results and cost levers; propose final config.

Can you confirm the proposed timeline and share the trace by tomorrow EOD? Also note if SSO/SCIM access or an internal approval is needed for the hosted test.

Thanks — rachel

Great — thanks for the clarifications and for sending the trace. Two quick operational notes before we run:

1) Test matrix we'll execute (initial run):
   - Short streaming flow (40–150 tokens): measure p50/p95/p99, per-token latency, and first-byte time.
   - Long completions (300–600 tokens): full completion latency and tail distribution.
   - Load shapes: steady 140 QPS / ramp to 400 / spike to 1100 for 10 mins / back to baseline.

2) Cost & perf levers we will evaluate in the run (we'll report delta per lever):
   - Continuous batching: tune max batch window and max batch size to trade latency vs throughput.
   - KV cache / prefix caching: measure hit rates using your chat history pattern; big wins for repeated prompts.
   - Quantization profiles: test fp16 -> int8 and int4 (where supported) and report quality delta vs token cost.
   - Model variants: try a lower-latency distilled variant for short-search streaming and a higher-quality variant for long completions; measure switch latency.
   - CPU offload tweaks: for streaming flows we'll exercise partial decode on CPU to reduce GPU contention.

Jordan will be running the bench and capturing kernel-level metrics so we can advise an initial config that meets your targets at minimum cost.

Proposed meeting: Thu 5/20 10:00 CET to review initial run. Does that work?

—Rachel

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical note on the cost/perf levers and the experimental plan I'm going to run: 

Planned bench variations (short):
- Baseline: current verified Redwood medium model (fp16), continuous batching enabled with 5ms window, no KV cache.
- Batching sweep: window 0ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms; batch size cap 8/16/32. Expect p95 to increase with larger windows but per-token cost to fall.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated-product lookups; expect 30–60% token reduction on hot paths.
- Quantization: fp16 vs int8 vs int4 (int4 only where accuracy drop <3% acceptable). We'll include an automated eval harness with a small labeled set you provided.
- Variant routing: test a low-latency variant (smaller transformer) for first-pass streaming; measure quality swing and model-switch latency (<50ms target).

Operational constraints to confirm from your side:
- Allowed test IPs (to open rate-limit exceptions).
- Any max token-length cutoff per request that we'd need to enforce.

Deliverables after run: csv of latency percentiles per sweep, per-lever cost estimate (USD/hour and USD/1M tokens), and recommended production config.

If you can confirm IPs and token cutoffs I'll kick off the first run this afternoon.

—Jordan
